name: Dana Reyes
tagline: B.S. Computer Science, Portland State University (June 2025). I build backend services and data pipelines, mostly in Python and Go. I like problems where the hard part is correctness under load rather than the feature itself, and I care about systems that stay debuggable at 3am.

bio.meta: B.S. Computer Science · Portland State University, June 2025
lead: Two years building and operating the ingestion pipeline behind a logistics product, where a late batch was a customer-visible failure rather than an internal one.
I am most useful on the seam between a service and its data: schemas, backfills, idempotency, and the retry logic nobody wants to own.
bio.close: Looking for backend or data platform work on a team that measures things.

highlights.title: Ingestion pipeline for logistics events
highlights.body: Rebuilt a nightly batch import as an incremental pipeline with idempotent writes, cutting the window from 40 minutes to under 4 and making a partial failure safe to rerun.

highlights.title: Job scheduler with exactly-once semantics
highlights.body: A Postgres-backed scheduler using advisory locks and a claim table, so a duplicated worker cannot run the same job twice. Documented the failure modes it does not cover.

highlights.title: Schema migration with no downtime
highlights.body: Moved a 90M row table to a new key layout using a dual-write and backfill, verified by a row-level diff before the cutover.

highlights.title: On-call runbooks that people actually used
highlights.body: Wrote the runbooks for the six alerts that paged most often, each naming the query to run first. Mean time to first useful action dropped noticeably.

stat.label: Runbooks written for the noisiest pages

highlights.title: This site
highlights.body: A grounded RAG chatbot over my own background: FastAPI, FAISS, a local embedding model, and a two pass drafter and judge pipeline so nothing unverified reaches the page.
